subject: Atrial flutter
object: typical and atypical types according to electrocardiographic characteristics and the circuit sustaining the arrhythmia.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: This classification system divides atrial flutter into two main types based on electrocardiographic characteristics and the circuit that sustains the arrhythmia: typical atrial flutter and atypical flutter.

subject: The epidemiology of atrial flutter
object: atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation can coexist.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: The epidemiology of atrial flutter (AFL) is not known with certainty, as atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation (AF) can coexist.

subject: People with atrial flutter
object: heart failure, stroke and all-cause mortality.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: Patients with atrial flutter are at increased risk for heart failure, stroke, and all-cause mortality .

subject: Prognosis differs between atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation: previous studies
relation: found adverse-event rates in atrial flutter to be
object: lower than in atrial fibrillation but higher than in healthy people without cardiac arrhythmias.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: There are prognostic differences between atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation. Previous studies have shown that the rate of adverse events in patients with atrial flutter is lower than in patients with atrial fibrillation, but still higher than in healthy individuals without cardiac arrhythmias .

subject: Typical atrial flutter
object: a reentrant circuit originating from the cavotricuspid isthmus and is currently the most prevalent macroreentrant arrhythmia.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: 2.1 Typical Atrial Flutter Characterized by a reentrant circuit originating from the CTI and is presently the most prevalent macroreentrant arrhythmia.

subject: In typical atrial flutter, the direction of depolarisation
object: counterclockwise flutter when the wavefront crosses the cavotricuspid isthmus, ascends the septal wall and descends the anterolateral right atrial wall; the opposite, less common direction is clockwise or reverse flutter.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: 2.1 Typical Atrial Flutter Depending on the direction of depolarization, it can be subclassified as counterclockwise, when the activation front passes through the CTI reaching the septal wall in a caudocranial direction and finally the anterolateral wall of the right atrium in a craniocaudal direction. Alternatively, it is referred to as clockwise or reverse when the activation front travels in the opposite direction, which is less common (Figs. 1, 2).

subject: Atypical atrial flutter
relation: is an atrial macroreentrant tachycardia whose circuit
object: does not depend on the cavotricuspid isthmus and can be in either the right or left atrium.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: 2.2 Atypical Flutter A type of atrial macroreentrant tachycardia that does not rely on the cavotricuspid isthmus circuit. Instead, this circuit can be located in either the right or left atrium.

subject: In atypical atrial flutter, circuit activation
object: around a surgical scar, after ablation or spontaneously; consequently it usually affects people with previous cardiac surgery or ablation, congenital heart disease, atrial fibrosis or cardiomyopathy.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: 2.2 Atypical Flutter Activation of the circuit often occurs around a surgical scar, after ablation, or even spontaneously (idiopathically). As a result, atypical flutter usually affects patients with a history of cardiac surgery, previous ablation, congenital heart disease, atrial fibrosis or cardiomyopathy .

subject: In atrial flutter, previous surgery or ablation, class IC antiarrhythmic drugs or structural heart disease
object: atypical findings, while some left atrial flutters can mimic the ECG morphology of typical flutter.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: It should be noted that previous procedures (surgery, ablation), drugs (class IC antiarrhythmics) or structural heart disease can cause atypical findings in patients with atrial flutter and, on the other hand, some left atrial flutters can mimic typical flutter electrocardiographic morphology.

subject: Macroreentry in the right atrium around the tricuspid annulus
object: approximately 75–80% of all atrial flutter cases.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: It is estimated that macroreentry in the right atrium around the tricuspid annulus accounts for approximately 75–80% of all cases of atrial flutter .

subject: The atrial flutter circuit
relation: has two barriers favouring its initiation and maintenance:
object: a posterior barrier formed by the crista terminalis and its continuation with the Eustachian valve, and an anterior barrier formed by the tricuspid annulus.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: The flutter circuit has two barriers that favor the genesis and maintenance of the arrhythmia: the posterior barrier of the activation wave is determined by the crista terminalis and its continuation with the Eustachian valve, while the anterior barrier is determined by the tricuspid annulus .

subject: In atrial flutter, the cavotricuspid isthmus
relation: has a crucial role in impulse propagation as
object: the circuit's slow-conduction zone, making it highly vulnerable to interval-dependent conduction block.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: The CTI plays a crucial role in the propagation of electrical impulses in atrial flutter, serving as the slow conduction zone of the circuit and therefore being highly vulnerable to interval-dependent conduction block .

subject: Atrial flutter is a reentrant arrhythmia with an excitable gap that can be transiently entrained or terminated by rapid atrial pacing; after an initial right atrial area is activated, the wavefront
object: slow-conducting tissue, allowing the initial atrial tissue to regain excitability and be reactivated; this recovered part of the circuit, the excitable gap, can be depolarised again so that the atrial impulse propagates.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: The main electrophysiological characteristics of atrial flutter can be summarized as a reentrant arrhythmia with an excitable gap that can be transiently entrained or terminated by rapid atrial pacing. As a reentrant arrhythmia, once an initial zone in the right atrium is activated, the wavefront spreads through an area of slow conduction that allows time for the initial atrial tissue to regain excitability, which is then re-activated. The excitable gap, which is the part of the reentrant circuit that has regained its excitability, can be depolarized again resulting in the propagation of the atrial impulse.

subject: A functional, unidirectional line of block between the two vena cava
relation: is hypothesised by some authors to be fundamental to
object: the initiation and maintenance of atrial flutter; it is theorised that episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation can trigger this line of block, which may then allow the onset of stable atrial flutter; without this unidirectional line of block, the patient will either remain in atrial fibrillation or return to sinus rhythm.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: Some authors support the hypothesis that a fundamental feature determining the genesis and maintenance of atrial flutter is the presence of a functional, unidirectional line of block between the two vena cava. It is theorized that episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation can trigger this line of block, which may then allow the onset of stable atrial flutter. Without this unidirectional line of block, the patient will either remain in atrial fibrillation or return to sinus rhythm .

subject: People with atrial flutter
relation: often have findings thought to be secondary to atrial remodelling, including
object: increased right atrial dilatation, prolonged ECG P-wave duration, sinus-node dysfunction and decreased voltage and impulse-conduction velocity on electrophysiological study.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: Patients with atrial flutter often exhibit many characteristic findings that are thought to be secondary to atrial remodeling, including increased right atrial dilatation, prolonged P wave duration on the electrocardiogram, sinus node dysfunction, and decreased voltage and conduction velocity of the electrical impulse in electrophysiological study .

subject: Known risk factors for developing atrial flutter
object: advanced age, alcohol consumption, arterial hypertension, diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and participation in high-intensity sports.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: In addition, there are many known risk factors for developing atrial flutter, including advanced age, alcohol consumption, arterial hypertension, diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and engaging in high-intensity sports .

subject: Atrial flutter
object: some structural heart disease, but 15–20% of cases occur without apparent structural heart disease.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: This arrhythmia usually arises in patients with some degree of structural heart disease; however, 15–20% of cases that develop atrial flutter have no apparent structural heart disease .

subject: Atrial flutter
object: palpitations, dyspnoea and asthenia, and less often chest pain, syncope and hypotension; these manifestations typically result from the increased ventricular response.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: Atrial flutter is mainly associated with symptoms such as palpitations, dyspnea, asthenia and to a lesser extent, chest pain, syncope and hypotension. These clinical manifestations are typically a result of the increased ventricular response associated with atrial flutter.

subject: In typical counterclockwise atrial flutter, inferior-to-superior activation of the right atrial septum
object: negative inferior-lead waves with a slow downward and rapid upward slope and positive V1 waves with craniocaudal lateral-wall activation, without an isoelectric line; these F waves have a cycle length of 250–170 milliseconds (240–350 beats per minute), whereas clockwise flutter reverses the pattern to positive inferior-lead and negative V1 waves; both patterns are sawtooth, especially in DII, DIII and aVF, and may be altered after surgery, catheter ablation or antiarrhythmic treatment.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: Given that the activation wave moves from the inferior to the superior right atrium septum, typical counterclockwise flutter is characterized electrocardiographically by the presence of negative waves with a slow downward slope followed by a rapid upward slope in the inferior leads and positive in V1 (coinciding with craneocaudal lateral wall activation) with no isoelectric line between them. These waves, known as “F” waves, have a cycle length between 250–170 milliseconds (240–350 beats per minute) (Fig. 3). In contrast, typical clockwise flutter is characterized by an inverted electrocardiographic pattern with positive waves in the inferior leads and negative waves in V1. Both patterns have been described as simulating a “sawtooth” pattern and are particularly evident in DII, DIII, and aVF . These characteristic findings may be altered in patients who have undergone cardiac surgery, catheter ablation or who are treated with antiarrhythmic drugs .

subject: The ECG of atypical atrial flutter
object: absent P waves and uniform flutter waves; unlike typical flutter, an isoelectric line may appear if conduction is significantly delayed, and some patients have concordant F-wave polarity in the inferior leads and V1.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: The electrocardiogram of atypical atrial flutter is identified by the following features: absence of P waves, presence of flutter waves with uniform morphology; unlike typical atrial flutter, an isoelectric line may be visible in some cases if conduction is significantly delayed, and in certain cases, patients with atypical atrial flutter may display concordance in the polarity of F waves in both inferior leads and V1.

subject: The ECG diagnosis of atrial flutter
object: atrial rather than ventricular activity, because different degrees of atrioventricular block can produce irregular ventricular rates.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: It is important to emphasize that the electrocardiographic diagnosis of flutter should be based on atrial activity, not ventricular activity, since different degrees of atrioventricular block may cause irregular ventricular rates.

subject: People with atrial flutter
object: serious secondary complications such as heart failure, myocardial ischaemia, tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy, stroke or systemic embolism.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: It is important to note that patients with atrial flutter may develop serious secondary complications, such as heart failure, myocardial ischemia, tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy, stroke, or systemic embolism .

subject: Atrial flutter
object: during the perioperative period of cardiac surgery or as a late complication.
source: Article: Abdala-Lizarraga J, Quesada-Ocete J, Quesada-Ocete B et al. Cavotricuspid Isthmus-Dependent Atrial Flutter. Beyond Simple Linear Ablation. Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2024
source_quote: Atrial flutter can manifest during the perioperative period of cardiac surgery or as a late complication.
